parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The student measures, and records in Table 1.1, the unstretched length l of the spring. He
does not include the loops at the ends of the spring in the measurement. The value l is the
length of the spring when the load L on the spring is 0.00 N.
Describe one technique you would use to obtain an accurate value for l . Draw a diagram to
illustrate your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The student suspends a load L = 1.00 N from the spring. He records the new length l of the
spring in Table 1.1.
He calculates the extension e of the spring using the equation e = (l – l ) and records the
value of e in Table 1.1.
The student repeats the procedure using loads L = 2.00 N, 3.00 N, 4.00 N and 5.00 N.
The readings and results are recorded in Table 1.1.
Calculate the extension e of the spring using the equation e = (l – l ) when L = 5.00 N. Record
this value of e in Table 1.1.
Table 1.1
L/ N l/ cm e/ cm
0.00 2.1 0.0
1.00 6.0 3.9
2.00 10.6 8.5
3.00 14.9 12.8
4.00 19.3 17.2
5.00 23.7

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of L/ N (y-axis) against e/ cm (x-axis). Start both axes at the origin (0, 0).
Draw the best-fit line.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show all your working and indicate on the graph the
values you use.
G = ______

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
G is numerically equal to the spring constant k.
Record the value of k to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. Include
the unit.
k = ______

text: A student investigates the bending of composite strips of wood when they are loaded at one end.
The composite strips are made from identical layers of wood stuck together, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
Plan an experiment to investigate how much composite strips bend when they are loaded at one
end. Fig. 4.2 shows the set-up the student uses.
The student has a number of composite strips made with two or more layers of wood.
